pageCache.pageTitle: The St Marylebone CE Bridge School - Home
pageCache.text:
Kindness & Compassion, Patience, Harmony & Forgiveness, Wisdom, Peace and Gratitude
St Marylebone offers innovative education for pupils with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) for Speech, Language and Communication needs.
By nurturing Compassion, Kindness, Forgiveness and Peace we have created a calm, safe and enjoyable learning environment where everyone matters and in which our pupils regularly experience success. A broad and balanced curriculum guarantees that our pupils access a range of qualifications that foster academic success, independence and social awareness while ensuring that every pupil reaches their full potential.
Open Afternoon and World Culture Celebration
Activities Week 2026
Year 7 Artwork Exhibited at The Wallace Collection
Chess Fest 2026
What We Offer
Speech and Language Therapy
Speech and language therapists work closely with school staff to ensure our school is a communication friendly environment.
Occupational Therapy
We work in collaboration with Westminster Training & Outreach Service Occupational Therapy Team to provide Occupational Therapy (OT) at a targeted and specialist level within the school.
Our Curriculum
Our pupils access a broad and balanced curriculum which is differentiated to meet individual learning needs and styles.
Extended Home Learning
Home-learning includes a whole range of things, not just things which are written down. It will vary for each child and is likely to change as a pupil gets older, develops or if their needs and priorities change.
Herries Street, London, W10 4LE

pageCache.pageTitle: The St Marylebone CE Bridge School - Curriculum Aims
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Aims
At the St Marylebone CE Bridge School (SMBS), our curriculum is differentiated to meet the needs of our pupils and to offer the appropriate level of challenge for our pupils’ individual stages of development.
The curriculum at SMBS fosters curiosity, creativity, enjoyment and ambition, enabling our students to reach their academic and language potential alongside developing their personal and spiritual understanding and positive mental health and wellbeing.
Our curriculum supports students to develop a deeper understanding of themselves and their strengths and difficulties in order to take their next steps in modern life, study and work with confidence and empower them to be active participants in their communities.
We respect and invest in subject specialism, promoting passion for what makes each subject worthy of study in its own right, while encouraging links between subjects.
Browse the individual subject Curriculum Aims to find out more information about what we offer.
Herries Street, London, W10 4LE

pageCache.pageTitle: The St Marylebone CE Bridge School - Computing Aims
pageCache.text:
Computing Aims
The computing curriculum at SMBS aims to ensure students:
To develop an understanding of the use, impact, and influence of technology in the modern world, and its role in shaping society, work, and everyday life.
To develop computational thinking through the effective use of new and existing technologies, encouraging logical reasoning, creativity, and independent problem solving.
To develop analytical and critical thinking skills through computational problem solving and the evaluation of digital solutions.
To engage in practical experiences of designing, creating, and writing computer programs (both visual and text-based), enabling pupils to solve problems creatively and independently.
To experience and apply the fundamental concepts of computing, including abstraction, logic, algorithms, and data representation, building transferable life skills for a rapidly evolving technological future.
To prepare pupils for a technological future that is constantly changing, equipping them with adaptability, resilience, and lifelong learning skills.
To develop digital literacy, enabling pupils to express, communicate, and develop ideas confidently through information and communication technology, including strong digital oracy skills.
To enable pupils to become active, responsible, and informed participants in the digital world, capable of collaborating, communicating, and creating using technology.
To develop the skills, knowledge, and experiences in computing and related technologies that prepare pupils for further education, employment, and adult life as confident, capable, and independent individuals.
To ensure pupils use technology safely, respectfully, responsibly, and securely in a wide range of contexts, understanding how to protect their online identity and personal data.
To develop pupils’ ability to recognise inappropriate content, contact, and conduct, and to know how to respond to and report concerns effectively.
All pupils will experience this entitlement, and the majority will have the opportunity to gain a qualification in Computing.
Herries Street, London, W10 4LE

pageCache.pageTitle: The St Marylebone CE Bridge School - School Ethos
pageCache.text:
School Ethos
The St. Marylebone CE Bridge School, a co-educational Church of England Special Free School, aims to create an environment in which our pupils can achieve their maximum potential, gain independence and social awareness so that they can enjoy and participate in the world of work and adult society along with their mainstream peers.
As a church school we nurture respect for religious, moral and spiritual values. These values are located within scripture in Colossians 3.12-17, and underpin all we believe in. We seek to nurture Compassion, Kindness, Patience, Forgiveness, Thankfulness, Wisdom, Peace and Gratitude in our school community. We acknowledge our special responsibility in promoting British values and in the education of students, so that they can take a full part in society.
Herries Street, London, W10 4LE

pageCache.text:
SEND Information Report
1. Who are the best people to talk to about my child’s needs?
To contact a staff member, please contact the school office in the first instance, at office@stmarylebonebridgeschool.com and they will direct your query to the appropriate person.
2. How does the school identify and support special educational needs?
Pupils at SMBS are supported in the following ways:
Small teaching groups.
3. How will the school let me know if there are any concerns about my child's learning, special educational needs or disability?
4. How will the school consider my views and those of my child in relation to their learning, special educational needs or disability?
5. How does the school assess and review my child's progress?
6. How will the school support my child to transition through different phases of education?
7. How does SMBS ensure that staff are trained appropriately to support my child's special educational needs or disability?
8. How will the school adapt the curriculum and learning environment to support my child's special educational needs or disability?
9. How will my child be taught at SMBS to ensure that their individual needs are met?
10. How will SMBS support my child's wellbeing and happiness?
11. How will the school help me to support my child's learning?
12. How will my child be included in all the same activities as their peers at school?
13. Who can I contact if I have a complaint about the SEND provision made for my child?
Initially speak with your child’s Form Tutor.
14. Who can I contact if I have any other questions about my child at SMBS?
Herries Street, London, W10 4LE
Email Usoffice@stmarylebonebridgeschool.com
